# ESPN Unlimited and Select prices, yearly and in bundles

 Updated October 6, 2026 · 4 min read · By The EvenOut team 

Quick answer

As of October 2026, ESPN Unlimited costs $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year, and ESPN Select costs $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year, before tax. The yearly plans save $63.89 and $27.89. ESPN bundles with Disney+ and Hulu start at $21.99 a month. A household that shares one plan can log it once with EvenOut's Repeat.

Key points

- ESPN Unlimited is $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year, and ESPN Select is $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year, as of October 2026, before tax.
- The yearly plan saves $63.89 on Unlimited (12 times $31.99 is $383.88) and $27.89 on Select (12 times $13.99 is $167.88).
- The Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundle is $8.99 a month less than the Disney+, Hulu Bundle plus ESPN Unlimited alone, and with Select it is $4.99 less.
- Anyone who subscribed before August 20, 2026 keeps their current price until their first billing date after September 17, 2026.
- EvenOut has no daily expense limit on its free plan and no ads, and its Repeat adds a shared plan's bill each month or year.

On this page

1. What do ESPN Unlimited and ESPN Select cost?
2. How much does the yearly plan save?
3. When do current subscribers move to these prices?
4. What do the Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundles cost?
5. What else includes ESPN?
6. How do you split an ESPN plan in one household?
7. Frequently asked questions

## What do ESPN Unlimited and ESPN Select cost?

As of October 2026, ESPN Unlimited is $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year, and ESPN Select is $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year. These are US dollars before tax, as listed on ESPN’s and Disney’s US pages in October 2026. Streaming prices change, so check the figure on the checkout page before you commit.

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly | Yearly saving |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESPN Unlimited | $31.99 | $319.99 | $63.89 |
| ESPN Select | $13.99 | $139.99 | $27.89 |

## How much does the yearly plan save?

The yearly plan saves about 16.6 percent on both tiers. Twelve months of Unlimited at $31.99 is $383.88, and $383.88 minus $319.99 is $63.89. Twelve months of Select at $13.99 is $167.88, and $167.88 minus $139.99 is $27.89.

The yearly price is about 10 months of monthly payments: 10 times $31.99 is $319.90, and 10 times $13.99 is $139.90. So the yearly plan is cheaper than paying monthly only if you would keep ESPN for 11 months or more.

## When do current subscribers move to these prices?

ESPN’s support page says anyone who subscribed before August 20, 2026 keeps their current price until their first billing date after September 17, 2026. Your billing date decides when you move to the prices above.

Take a monthly subscriber who joined in July and is billed on the 20th. The first billing date after September 17 was September 20, 2026, so that bill was the first at the new rate. Someone billed on the 5th reached it on October 5, 2026.

## What do the Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundles cost?

Each ESPN bundle costs less than the Disney+, Hulu Bundle plus the same ESPN plan on its own. The Disney+, Hulu Bundle is $12.99, or $21.99 for Premium. All figures are monthly, in US dollars, before tax, as of October 2026.

| Bundle | Bundle price | Disney+, Hulu Bundle plus ESPN alone | You save |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited | $35.99 | $44.98 | $8.99 |
| Same, Premium version | $44.99 | $53.98 | $8.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select | $21.99 | $26.98 | $4.99 |
| Same, Premium version | $32.99 | $35.98 | $2.99 |

The Disney+, Hulu Bundle also has a lower price for the first 6 months, $11.99 or $19.99 for Premium. The savings above use the regular prices, not the first-6-months prices.

Two more offers carry an ESPN plan, and Disney’s pages list both with their own prices:

# ESPN Select vs ESPN Unlimited: Which One Do You Need for Live Sports?

ESPN sells two streaming plans. Select is the old ESPN+ library for $13.99 a month, and Unlimited adds the actual ESPN networks for $31.99 a month. We break down what each one carries, what the bundles cost, whether your TV provider already gives you Unlimited, and which plan fits which kind of fan.

Founder & Editor · TVLander

IN THIS ARTICLE

TL;DR

- ESPN Select costs $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year and includes the full ESPN+ library, including NHL Power Play out-of-market hockey.
- ESPN Unlimited costs $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year and adds ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ABC's ESPN games, SEC Network, ACC Network, NFL Network and more.
- The Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle is $35.99 a month with ads, only $4 more than Unlimited alone.
- Many pay-TV packages (YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, DIRECTV, Fubo, Spectrum, Xfinity and others) can include ESPN Unlimited at no extra charge once you activate it.
- Pick Select for out-of-market NHL, LALIGA, Bundesliga and PGA TOUR LIVE. Pick Unlimited for college football, Monday Night Football, the NBA and anything on the ESPN channels.

A smartphone, a streaming remote and a tablet laid out on a dark marble table, both screens glowing with blurred red and blue sports light

ESPN's streaming lineup comes down to two plans, and the names don't tell you much. ESPN Select is basically ESPN+ under a new name. ESPN Unlimited is the full thing: every ESPN network, live, in the ESPN app, no cable box needed. The price gap is real ($13.99 versus $31.99 a month), so it pays to know which games actually live where before you sign up.

The short version: if you mostly watch out-of-market hockey, European soccer or golf, Select probably covers you. If you want college football Saturdays, Monday Night Football or the NBA on ESPN, you need Unlimited, or a TV package that already includes it.

## How much do ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited cost?

ESPN Select is $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year, and ESPN Unlimited is $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year, according to ESPN's plans and prices page. Paying annually saves you about $28 a year on Select and about $64 on Unlimited compared with twelve monthly payments.

| | ESPN Select | ESPN Unlimited |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price | $13.99 | $31.99 |
| Annual price | $139.99 | $319.99 |
| What it is | The full ESPN+ library | Everything in Select plus all ESPN networks |
| ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes | No | Yes |
| ESPN on ABC | No | Yes |
| SEC Network, ACC Network, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra | No | Yes |
| NFL Network | No | Yes |
| NHL Power Play (out-of-market NHL) | Yes | Yes |
| ESPN+ exclusive NHL games | Yes | Yes |
| ESPN and ABC national NHL games | No | Yes |
| ESPN 4K HDR | No (no ESPN channels) | Yes, on supported devices |
| Watch in Disney+ | Yes, with Disney+ | Yes, with Disney+ |
| Included with some pay-TV packages | No | Yes, after activation |

Prices are before tax. Paying annually only makes sense if you'll actually use the plan year-round. A hockey-only fan, for example, needs about seven months of service, which is cheaper month to month.

## What does ESPN Select include?

ESPN Select includes the full ESPN+ library and nothing from the traditional ESPN channels. Disney+'s live sports help page lists NHL, PGA TOUR LIVE, Grand Slam tennis, college sports from the Big 12, SEC, ACC and The American, international soccer like LALIGA, Bundesliga, FA Cup and Carabao Cup, plus the complete 30 for 30 library.

For hockey fans, Select is the sneaky good deal. ESPN says NHL Power Play carries more than 1,050 out-of-market games in 2026-27, with a choice of home or away commentary, and it's "available to all ESPN DTC subscribers." Disney+ spells it out too: out-of-market NHL games require "any standalone ESPN subscription," so Select gets you in. You also get the 47 national NHL games

# ESPN Hikes Streaming Prices: ESPN Select and Unlimited Get New Rates in the US

ESPN hikes streaming prices in the United States starting September 17, 2026, increasing the monthly cost of both its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited direct-to-consumer plans. The price change comes as the sports network continues expanding its streaming-focused strategy and offering more live sports directly to consumers without requiring a traditional pay-TV subscription.

According to ESPN’s official customer support information, ESPN Select now costs $13.99 per month, while ESPN Unlimited is priced at $31.99 per month. Annual subscription prices are also listed at $139.99 for Select and $319.99 for Unlimited.

The new rates represent an increase from the earlier $13 monthly price for Select and $30 monthly price for Unlimited.

## ESPN Select and Unlimited Prices Increase

The two ESPN plans are designed for different types of sports viewers.

ESPN Select is the lower-priced option and consists entirely of ESPN+ content. Subscribers can access thousands of live sporting events and programming covering sports such as soccer, golf, hockey, college sports and tennis, along with ESPN Originals and other on-demand content.

The new monthly price is $13.99, compared with the previous $13 rate.

ESPN Unlimited, meanwhile, provides a substantially broader package. It includes ESPN Select content as well as ESPN’s network programming and services, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC and other ESPN services.

The Unlimited monthly price has increased to $31.99, up from $30.

### ESPN Streaming Price Changes

| Plan | Previous Monthly Price | New Monthly Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESPN Select | $13 | $13.99 |
| ESPN Unlimited | $30 | $31.99 |

The annual prices are now $139.99 for ESPN Select and $319.99 for ESPN Unlimited.

## Existing Subscribers Get a Transition Period

The price increase does not necessarily mean every existing customer was charged the new amount immediately on September 17.

ESPN says customers who subscribed before August 20, 2026, retain their previous price until their first billing date after September 17. This means the actual date when an existing subscriber sees the higher charge can depend on their individual billing cycle.

New subscribers, meanwhile, are subject to the current prices listed by ESPN.

The change applies to monthly and annual direct subscriptions, although annual subscribers generally remain on their existing plan terms until renewal.

## What ESPN Select Includes

ESPN Select is essentially the new home for the ESPN+ experience.

The service includes ESPN+ programming and a large collection of live and on-demand sports. ESPN says Select subscribers can watch content covering soccer, PGA TOUR events, NHL games, college sports, tennis and other programming.

ESPN+ itself has not been discontinued.

Instead, existing ESPN+ subscribers were transitioned into ESPN Select while continuing to receive access to the ESPN+ content they previously received.

For viewers who primarily want ESPN’s streaming library and selected live sports rather than the complete network lineup, Select remains the lower-cost direct subscription.

## What ESPN Unlimited Includes

ESPN Unlimited is designed for viewers who want access to the broader ESPN ecosystem.

The package includes everything available through Select plus the company’s wider collection of networks and services. ESPN lists ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN+, ESPN on ABC, ESPN3, SEC Network+ and ACCNX among the services available through Unlimited.

# How to Watch ESPN Without Cable in 2026

October 4, 2026

Written By: 

Jim Kimble

 

Some links below are affiliate links; I may earn a commission if you buy through them.

ESPN is a cable sports channel, but you no longer need a cable, satellite or live TV streaming provider to watch it.

In 2026, Sling Essentials is the cheapest way to stream ESPN each month. The $19.99 plan includes ESPN and ESPN2.

ESPN Unlimited is the direct-to-consumer option if you want the full ESPN channel lineup without a TV provider. Unlimited costs $31.99 per month or $319.99 per year.

The Unlimited plan includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ACC Network, SEC Network, ESPNEWS and ESPN Deportes, along with ESPN on ABC, ACCNX and SECN+.

You can also get ESPN through live TV streaming services such as Sling TV, Fubo, DIRECTV, Hulu + Live TV and YouTube TV. Those services bundle ESPN with larger channel lineups that can include local stations, news and other sports networks.

You won’t find ESPN on Peacock, Amazon Prime or Paramount Plus. And you can’t watch ESPN with a TV antenna because ESPN is a cable channel. 

A TV antenna can still give you local ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC and PBS stations for free. That matters for sports because NFL games, college football, MLB, NBA and other major events still air on broadcast TV throughout the year.

You can watch ESPN without cable through ESPN Unlimited, Sling TV, Fubo, DIRECTV, YouTube TV and Hulu + Live TV.

ESPN Unlimited is different from the other services because it comes directly from ESPN rather than a TV provider. 

Sling, Fubo, DIRECTV, YouTube TV and Hulu bundle ESPN with other live channels, including sports, news, entertainment and, on some plans, local ABC, CBS, FOX and NBC stations.

ESPN is raising prices on Unlimited and Select plans — here's how to avoid the increase or get the service for free

## There are some ways to keep streaming everything on ESPN Unlimited at no extra cost.

Danica Creahan, Liz Kocan

Thu, September 17, 2026 at 7:57 PM UTC

View larger image

Here's how to save a few bucks and avoid the new ESPN price increases. (Choreograph (Konstantin Yuganov) via Getty Images)

ESPN Unlimited is ESPN's premium streaming tier, which launched in 2025. Initially, the service cost subscribers $29.99/month (or $299.99/year) for access to all of ESPN's linear networks, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SECN, ACCN, ESPNews and ESPN Deportes, plus access to programming on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX. A less-expensive option, ESPN Select, which is essentially a more robust version of the old ESPN+, also launched, costing $12.99/month.

But as is customary with all streaming services, those initial rates weren't going to last forever, and this week, ESPN announced that its Unlimited plan price has increased to $31.99/month, or $319.99/year, and the Select plan is now $13.99/month, or $139.99/year.

While we do love the fact that an ESPN Unlimited plan provides access to thousands of live events and other original programming, all of these increases take a toll on the old wallet. Fortunately, there are a few ways to make things hurt a little less. ESPN Unlimited is actually included in the price of several live TV streaming services like Fubo and DirecTV, cable providers like Spectrum, or you can bundle it with other platforms like FOX One to save big on monthly fees.

Here are some of the best ways to avoid ESPN's new price increases or get the plan for free!

DIRECTV offers several packages at all different price tiers, but if you want to get ESPN Unlimited included in one of them, you'll need to sign up for either their Choice, Ultimate or Premier packages (see all the plan descriptions and offerings here). Prices start at $64.99/month for your first month, and you'll also get unlimited Cloud DVR storage and access to Disney+, Hulu (with ads) included in each of these plans.

If you're a sports fanatic with little use for news or entertainment channels, DIRECTV's MySports Genre Pack costs even less, just $44.99 for your first 6 months, and it includes ESPN Unlimited along with 20+ additional sports channels. You can also try out any plan for free for five days.

### Save with a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundle

### Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited 

We're fans of the Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited bundle; even though it's pricey at $35.99/month, it's a must-have for its vast array of sports and entertainment offerings, and even though ESPN just raised their subscription rates, the cost of the bundle hasn't increased.

(Football fans, take note: You can also add a subscription to NFL+ Premium to the bundle and pay $45.99/month. That's a $5/month savings, considering that a standalone NFL+ Premium subscription costs $14.99/month. A subscription to NFL+ Premium gets you live local & primetime regular season and postseason games on your phone or tablet, access to the NFL Network, live out-of-market preseason games, live game audio for every game, plus NFL Red Zone, NFL Pro, and full game replays.)

### Save with an ESPN Unlimited/FOX One bundle

# ESPN Unlimited Price Increase: How to Keep Watching Without Paying More 

 September 19, 2026

By Phillip Swann The TV Answer Man Follow me on X or Facebook

Table of Contents

It was just a matter of time. The ESPN Unlimited price increase has arrived. Yes, ESPN yesterday (September 17, 2026) increased the monthly price of its ESPN Unlimited app from $29.99 to $31.99. The ESPN Select streaming service also increased from $12.99 a month to $13.99 a month.

This is the first time that ESPN has raised prices on the Unlimited app since its launch a year ago. But it continues an industry trend with streamers hiking rates to offset rising programming costs.

However, as always, TV For Seniors has your back. We have compiled three ways that you can keep watching ESPN and/or the Unlimited app without paying an extra cent.

### Use An Existing Pay TV Or Live TV Streaming Login

Many traditional cable/satellite providers and major live TV services (including recent additions like Comcast Xfinity and YouTube TV) allow eligible subscribers to unlock the full ESPN Unlimited experience directly in the ESPN app at no extra charge. Log in with your provider credentials in the ESPN app or on stream.espn.com. This can be the easiest (and cheapest) option if you already pay for a package that includes ESPN channels.

The List of TV Providers Who Offer ESPN Unlimited For Free

- Comcast Xfinity
- Cox
- DIRECTV
- Fubo
- Hulu + Live TV
- Spectrum
- U-verse
- Verizon FiOS
- YouTube TV

### Get Sling TV’s Essentials Plan

If you mainly need the flagship linear networks (ESPN, ESPN2, etc.) rather than the full Unlimited extras, Sling TV’s Essential package could be your answer. The plan includes ESPN, ESPN 2 and 11 other channels for just $19.99 a month. See our article for more details.

### Stay With the ESPN/Disney Plus/Hulu Bundle

If you have the ESPN Unlimited/Disney Plus/Hulu ads-included bundle, the price ($35.99 a month) is not increasing. So while the package costs more than ESPN Unlimited standalone, at least you won’t have to pay more over what you’re currently paying.

### What Is ESPN Unlimited?

ESPN Unlimited is ESPN’s premium streaming app which was launched in August 2025. The service includes all ESPN live channels and on-demand programming so you don’t need ESPN in a traditional pay TV package.

Subscribers get ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network), ESPN on ABC sports, NFL Network, plus all former ESPN+ content—live events, studio shows like SportsCenter and College GameDay, originals, and on-demand replays. It covers tens of thousands of live games and events yearly across NFL, NBA, college sports, NHL, and more.

### What Is ESPN Select?

ESPN Select is the more affordable tier of ESPN’s direct-to-consumer streaming service and it was launched in 2025 as the successor to ESPN+.

It focuses on digital-exclusive and select live events rather than all the live ESPN channels. Subscribers get thousands of live games and events (including some college sports, NHL, MLS, UFC, golf, tennis, and more), ESPN Originals, 30 for 30 documentaries, on-demand content, and studio programming. However, you don’t getESPN, ESPN2, SEC Network, ACC Network, or most major-network NFL/NBA games that air on the live ESPN channels available on cable/satellite TV plans.

By the PickMyStream Editorial Desk. Prices and availability as of September 2026.

# How to stream ESPN without cable in 2026

Pictured: The Kingdom. Image via TMDB.

Cutting the cord used to mean giving up live sports. Not anymore. ESPN now sells its channels and its streaming content directly to you, no cable subscription required, and the choice comes down to two plans with two very different jobs.

This guide breaks down ESPN streaming the honest way. What ESPN Select actually carries, what ESPN Unlimited adds, what each costs as of September 26, 2026, the devices that run the app, and the bundles where ESPN Unlimited already comes attached to something you might buy anyway. By the end you will know exactly which plan matches how you watch.

## The two ESPN plans, explained

ESPN sells two plans direct, and the names tell you less than the contents do. ESPN Select is $13.99 monthly or $139.99 a year, as of September 26, 2026. This is the plan built entirely from ESPN+ content. Top-tier soccer, PGA TOUR, NHL, college sports and a selection of other ESPN programming. If you remember ESPN+, this is where that content lives now.

One thing Select does not do is carry the ESPN cable channel itself. The networks’ live broadcasts and studio shows like SportsCenter sit in Unlimited, not here. Select is for the streaming-first sports fan who wants soccer, golf and college coverage without paying for the full channel lineup.

ESPN Unlimited is the bigger swing at $31.99 monthly or $319.99 a year, as of September 26, 2026. It includes all of the ESPN networks plus ESPN+: ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra, NFL Network and CW Sports.

If you signed up before August 20, 2026, ESPN says you keep your old price until your first billing date after September 17, 2026. Worth checking your account if you are a longtime subscriber before you assume the new numbers apply to you.

## What ESPN Unlimited actually carries

This is the plan that replaces cable for most sports households. ESPN lists NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, tennis and golf majors, WWE, and SEC, ACC and Big 12 football and basketball. The studio shows are here too: SportsCenter, First Take and College GameDay.

Postseason is where Unlimited earns its price. ESPN lists postseason coverage from the NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB and the College Football Playoff. That is a full calendar of live sports, not a highlights service.

One caveat matters if you activate through a TV provider rather than buying direct. ESPN notes that when Unlimited is activated through a provider, content the provider does not carry may be missing. Buying direct from ESPN avoids that gap.

## The devices that run ESPN

ESPN's app is nearly everywhere. Per ESPN's supported devices page, it runs on Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV (4th generation and later), Chromecast, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox and Android TV, plus smart TVs from Hisense, LG webOS, Samsung Tizen and Vizio SmartCast, along with Xumo TV and the XiOne Box.

It also reaches into existing provider hardware: Xfinity Flex and X1 boxes and Cox Contour. On the go, the ESPN app covers iPhone and iPad, Android phones and tablets, Amazon Fire tablets, Windows 10 and 11 computers, and any modern web browser.

In short, if you own a recent smart TV or one of the mainstream streaming devices above, you can watch. There is no special box to buy just for ESPN.

## Where ESPN Unlimited comes bundled

You do not always have to buy ESPN on its own. Per Disney's bundle page, read September 26, 2026, the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle is $35.99 monthly, pairing Disney+ with ads, Hulu with ads and ESPN Unlimited with ads. The Premium version is $44.99 monthly, which drops the ads on Disney+ and Hulu while keeping ESPN Unlimited with ads.

- Most non-NFL sports fans only need Select. College sports, soccer, UFC, golf, and tennis are almost entirely an ESPN+ library, which Select already includes.
- Unlimited only pays for itself if you watch the live channels — Monday Night Football, SEC/ACC Network game windows, or NFL Network — none of which Select carries at any price.
- If you subscribed before August 20, 2026, you keep the old price until your next billing cycle after the increase lands.

ESPN quietly raised prices on both its streaming tiers effective September 17, 2026 — right as the fall sports calendar (college football conference play, the start of the NFL and NHL seasons) kicks into gear. If you’re deciding whether to sign up, downgrade, or just eat the increase, the two tiers aren’t actually the same service at two price points. Here’s what each one gets you.

## What changed on September 17, 2026

ESPN’s streaming lineup has two standalone tiers, both of which got more expensive this month:

| Plan | Old monthly | New monthly | Old annual | New annual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESPN Select | $12.99 | $13.99 | $129.99 | $139.99 |
| ESPN Unlimited | $29.99 | $31.99 | $299.99 | $319.99 |

It’s the first price change for Unlimited since it launched, and the second increase for Select (it started life as ESPN+ at $11.99). If you were already subscribed before August 20, 2026, you’re grandfathered in at the old price until your first billing date after September 17 — so the increase doesn’t hit everyone the same week.

The Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundles moved too, since ESPN’s tiers are one of the three ingredients: the ad-supported Select bundle went from $19.99 to $21.99/month, and the ad-free version from $29.99 to $32.99. If you’re weighing the bundle math on top of picking a tier, see our streaming bundles guide — the “worth it if you’d use all three apps anyway” logic still holds, just at slightly higher numbers.

## Select vs. Unlimited: what you actually get

The names suggest Unlimited is just “more of Select,” but the split is really streaming-only library vs. streaming-plus-live-channels:

ESPN Select is the ESPN+ content library: college football and basketball (a large slate, though not every nationally televised game), top-flight international soccer, the PGA Tour, NHL out-of-market games, UFC pay-per-view-adjacent content, tennis, and a long tail of niche sports ESPN+ has carried for years. It does not include the live ESPN or ESPN2 cable-style channel feed.

ESPN Unlimited includes everything in Select, plus the actual linear channels: ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network (and their “Extra”/”+” companion feeds), ESPN’s simulcast of ABC’s sports coverage, and NFL Network. That’s where Monday Night Football lives, along with the biggest nationally-televised college football windows and NFL Network’s own game slate — none of which Select carries, at any price.

The practical way to think about it: Select is “the ESPN app as a sports library,” Unlimited is “the ESPN app plus the cable channels you’d otherwise need a live-TV service for.”

Jimmy Pitaro Wants ESPN to Be the First Stop for NFL Fans | Observer

# Jimmy Pitaro Built ESPN’s Streaming Future. But How Many Fans Are Paying for It?

## Jimmy Pitaro is turning ESPN Unlimited into an NFL streaming hub with NFL Network, fantasy football and a Super Bowl, even without every game.

 By Mónica Marie Zorrilla • 09/24/26 11:52am

Jimmy Pitaro recently called the timing of ESPN’s streaming launch one of the hardest decisions of his life. Thirteen months later, the compromise is visible everywhere in the app. Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images

ESPN is getting closer to being the place NFL fans can start without first checking four other apps. Unlimited now puts Monday Night Football and NFL Network under one roof. It still can’t give you the whole season: CBS and FOX own most Sunday afternoons, NBC has Sunday Night Football, and Amazon carries Thursday nights. 

ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro spent years deciding when the sports network could afford this. At the Fast Company Innovation Festival last week, Pitaro called the timing of its direct-to-consumer launch “one of the most challenging” decisions of his life. ESPN wanted a direct relationship with viewers without blowing up the pay-TV business that still delivers millions of households. 

NFL Network is inside the ESPN app, and customers of participating pay-TV providers can activate Unlimited without buying a separate ESPN subscription.

Pitaro does not pretend that ESPN can buy every sports right. What he wants instead is for the app to be the “starting point” for sports fans. 

### The numbers Disney gives, and the ones it doesn’t

Unlimited launched in August 2025 at $29.99 per month or $299.99 per year. It now costs $31.99 per month or $319.99 per year. S ubscribers who signed up before Aug. 20 kept the old rate until their first billing date after Sept. 17.

When CNBC asked Pitaro about ESPN pricing in July, he recalled that the standalone Unlimited service and a Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundle had both launched at $29.99. “It was kind of an IQ test,” he said.

Disney still doesn’t disclose a subscriber count for Unlimited. Kevin Ota, ESPN’s senior director of communications, tells Observer that about 80 percent of Unlimited Subscribers access the service through Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited bundle.

Don’t blame Pitaro for keeping consumers in the dark. Bob Iger, then Disney’s chief executive, and Hugh Johnston, its finance chief, had already decided in 2025 to stop reporting ESPN+ subscriber numbers, arguing that those quarterly metrics were becoming less useful as its direct-to-consumer strategy changed. Unlimited launched after that decision.

For the three months ending June 27, Disney’s Sports segment generated $4.5 billion in revenue, up 4 percent from a year earlier. Operating income fell 17 percent to $858 million as programming and production costs rose, including contractual rate increases and new sports-rights costs. The segment covers the ESPN networks, the streaming service, NFL media assets and the international channels. It does not break out Unlimited on its own. 

Pitaro offered one fresh football number at Fast Company: ESPN’s fantasy business has crossed 16 million users, up 2 million from the prior year and a record for the fifth consecutive year. That number measures the reach of ESPN’s football business, not the number paying for Unlimited. 

One of the clearest public launch-period subscriber estimates comes from Antenna, which tracks streaming subscriptions using transaction data. It counted roughly 2.1 million U.S. ESPN sign-ups between Aug. 21 and Sept. 30, 2025, with 57 percent choosing Unlimited. Antenna’s estimate excludes existing Disney customers who changed plans and viewers who activated ESPN through a pay-TV provider. It also measures sign-ups, not current subscribers.
